findings.finding: The change is safe because a change to unowned files alone cannot hide source from a check. Ownership is half of that fact. .github/CODEOWNERS leaves only app and server source, tests, harness, assets, native iOS files, shared contracts, and skill records without an owner, and it gives back every dotfile, dot folder, *.config.* file, package manifest, lockfile, tsconfig, Podfile, Gemfile, and packages/app/src/config.example.ts at any depth. tools/__tests__/codeowners.test.js applies GitHub's last-match rule to every tracked file and to new files such as packages/server/src/.gitignore, packages/app/src/.npmrc, and packages/server/nitro.config.ts. The guards are the other half, because a check's own ignore list can skip unowned paths: verify.cjs pins the npm registry, npm run lint passes --disable-nested-config, the ignored-files check fails on a tracked file under a .gitignore path, the security check fails on source in a path that rnsec skips, and lint bans @ts-nocheck, @ts-ignore, and inline disables of typescript/ban-ts-comment. Two exceptions remain and docs/github-controls.md names them. The unowned project.pbxproj can add a Swift package, and the suppression policy allows a named inline lint disable with a reason in unowned source for other rules.

packages/app/App.tsx and packages/app/index.js are app source, so .github/CODEOWNERS now lists them in the unowned block, before the owned config lines. The controls rule lists both in excludePaths, because its packages/*/* glob would route them otherwise. codeowners.test.js expects no owner for both files and checks that they are not routed to controls. packages/app/app.json and packages/app/android/** keep the owner.

A project .npmrc could send the dependency audit to another registry. tools/verify.cjs now sets npm_config_registry for every check it runs, and npm ranks the environment above a project .npmrc. With a stub-registry .npmrc and the old environment, audit:check sent its bulk advisory request to the stub and failed. With the new variable, the stub got no request and audit:check passed against the public registry. verify:commit on a commit that adds the stub .npmrc on top of this range made no request to the stub.

A nested .oxlintrc.json replaced the root lint rules for its folder. With {} in packages/server/src/.oxlintrc.json and a line that breaks eqeqeq and the type-assertion rules in api.ts, oxlint without the flag exited 0. npm run lint now passes --disable-nested-config and exits 1 with those rules named. The only tracked .oxlintrc.json is the root one, so the flag changes nothing today.

No oxlint or oxfmt flag stops a nested .gitignore from hiding source. With src/ appended to packages/server/.gitignore, npm run lint still exits 0 on the probe line. Ownership is the control, so packages/server/.gitignore and any new nested .gitignore, .eslintignore, or .prettierignore now need owner review.

Docs, root files, package-root files such as packages/app/app.json, and packages/app/android now have the owner. The controls rule mirrors that set, so a change to them routes blast-radius, and a small edit to them no longer qualifies for the tiny tier. routing-committed.test.js now expects controls for docs edits, a readme plan, and skill edits, and a 2-line skill edit is no longer tiny.
findings.none: Intended by the owner-by-default rule, and the routing test pins it.

findings.finding: tools/github/integration-rules.json now equals the live ruleset, rule by rule, after adding the rebase-only merge method, the extra approval for unattributed changes, and the empty reviewer list. ruleset.cjs passes the parameters through unchanged, and ruleset.test.js still passes.

oxlint and oxfmt skip every path that .gitignore names, and **/coverage/** matched at any depth, so a tracked file in packages/server/src/coverage/, build/, or node_modules/ escaped lint and format. The coverage patterns now name only coverage/, packages/app/coverage/, and packages/server/coverage/, and a probe in packages/server/src/coverage/ is reported by both tools while packages/app/coverage/ stays ignored. The new ignored-files check runs git ls-files --cached --ignored --exclude-standard with an empty core.excludesFile, so a personal global ignore list cannot change its result. It lists no file on the clean head.

rnsec 1.3.0 skips a fixed list of paths (dist/core/fileWalker.js defaultIgnore) that no option removes, and the list is a local constant, so the check cannot import it. tools/security-check.cjs copies it, and hidden-source.test.js reads the list from rnsec's source and fails when the two differ. The check fails on tracked .js, .jsx, .ts, or .tsx files that match the list outside packages/app/__tests__/, packages/server/tests/, and tools/__tests__/. The guard lists the whole repo, although rnsec scans only packages/app, because the brief names the server and tools test folders. On the clean head no file matches.

oxlint applies an inline disable of a built-in rule under any plugin prefix or none. typescript/ban-ts-comment, @typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment, typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment, xyz/ban-ts-comment, and bare ban-ts-comment each turned the rule off. A JS plugin rule such as project/no-type-assertion needs its exact name. require-disable-reason therefore matches ban-ts-comment as the last part of any listed rule name, and lint-policy.test.js covers the prefixed, the @typescript-eslint, and the bare comma-joined forms.

A described @ts-expect-error in unowned source still suppresses the type error on its next line. The decided policy keeps it, because the one existing use in packages/server/tests/models.test.ts has a description, and tsc fails when the next line has no error. docs/github-controls.md says each @ts-expect-error needs a description.
findings.none: Allowed by the decided suppression policy, and the doc names it.
